NONE: › in cricket, six runs (= points) scored when the player hits the ball to the edge of the playing area without it touching the ground first

example: Look for a bus with a number six on the front of it.
找一輛前面有數字六的公車。
"How many grandchildren do you have now?" "I've got six."
「現在你有幾個孫兒孫女了？」「我有六個。」
Richards hit a six.
理查茲擊中了一個六分球。

NONE: › said when you think that neither of two choices is better than the other

example: "Shall we give her chocolates or flowers?" "I don't know, it's six of one and half a dozen of the other."
「我們應該送她巧克力還是花？」 「不知道，都差不多。」

NONE: › a beating, usually of six hits with a stick
一頓痛打（通常是用棍棒打六下）
› football played by two teams of six players, not the usual eleven players. The playing area is surrounded by a wall, not lines, and the game does not stop for throw-ins, corners, or goal kicks.
› a person who is at least six feet (1.83 metres) tall
身高六呎（1.83公尺）以上的人
› informal six containers, usually bottles or cans, of a particular type of beer or other drink that are sold together as one unit
（啤酒或其他飲料的）六瓶裝，六罐裝
› humorous the well-developed muscles of a man's stomach
（男子的）發達的腹肌； 六塊肌

› a football game, especially one at the end of a season between teams that are both near the top or bottom of a division, that has extra importance because winning not only gains three points, it also stops an opponent getting three points
六分比賽（足球聯賽期間，尤其在賽季末進行的兩支比分接近的球隊間的比賽，其重要性在於獲勝方不僅可贏得三分，而且同時可阻止對方贏得三分，造成六分的差距）
› a small gun that holds six bullets
› in football, the area surrounded by white lines inside the penalty area, within which a goal kick must be taken
› six times as big or as much

example: a sixfold rise in profit
利潤增長六倍
the snowflake's sixfold symmetry
雪花的六角形對稱

NONE: › a small, silver-coloured coin, used in the UK until 1971, that was worth six old pennies, or this amount of money

example: a sixpenny bit
一枚六便士硬幣
We have got sixteen (people) coming for lunch.
我們有16個人來吃午飯。
He dropped out of school at sixteen (= when he was 16 years old).
他16歲時輟學。

NONE: › one of 16 equal parts of something

example: Their anniversary is on the sixteenth (of June).
他們的紀念日是在（六月）十六日。
It weighs only a sixteenth of an ounce.
它的重量僅為十六分之一盎司。

NONE: › a musical note that has a time value of half a quaver or a 16th of a semibreve
› one of six equal parts of something

example: I have to return my library books on the sixth (of July).
我得在（7月）6號歸還圖書館的書。
Jim was/came sixth in the 100 metres.
吉姆在百米比賽中獲得第六。
Cut the cake into sixths.
把蛋糕切成六塊。

NONE: › in Britain, the part of a school for students aged 16-18
（英國學生年齡在16歲至18歲之間的）中學六年級

example: The sixth-form students are preparing to take their A levels.
中學六年級的學生正準備參加他們的高等程度考試。

NONE: › an ability that some people believe they have that seems to give them information without using the five senses of sight, hearing, touch, smell, or taste

example: A sixth sense told me that the train was going to crash.
直覺告訴我這列火車會撞車。

NONE: › a student in the sixth form
› A person's sixties are the period in which they are aged between 60 and 69
› the range of temperature between 60° and 69° Fahrenheit
六十多度（指華氏60到69度之間）
B2 the decade (= period of ten years) between 60 and 69 in any century, usually 1960–1969

example: Many people retire in their sixties.
許多人60多歲退休。

每年這個時候的氣溫通常都是華氏60多度。

披頭四樂隊在1960年代推出了他們首批風靡一時的唱片。

NONE: › one of 60 equal parts of something

example: fifty-nine, sixty, sixty-one

她打算在60歲時退休。

NONE: › sixty times as big or as much

example: a sixtyfold increase
六十倍的增長

處理器的操作頻率增加了六十倍。
